t: The problem: Git hates big files
title: The problem: Git hates big files
description: Git stores every version of every file forever, so committing 4GB model weights balloons clones and slows every operation. LFS exists because binaries break Git's assumptions. The problem statement motivates the tool.

demo.program: print('4GB weights in git -> every clone downloads every version')
demo.expected_output: 4GB weights in git -> every clone downloads every version

title: Pointer files: the core trick
description: LFS replaces big files in the repo with tiny pointer files (version, OID, size); actual content lives on the LFS server and downloads on demand. Git stays small; content stays versioned. The pointer is the indirection.

demo.program: print('pointer: version + OID + size; content on LFS server')
demo.expected_output: pointer: version + OID + size; content on LFS server

title: .gitattributes: what gets tracked
description: *.gguf filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text in .gitattributes routes matching files to LFS. Tracking is pattern-based and committed. One file declares the policy.

title: git lfs track and install
description: git lfs install sets up the filters once per machine; git lfs track '*.bin' registers patterns. Two commands enable everything. Setup is a minute.

demo.program: print('git lfs install && git lfs track "*.gguf"')
demo.expected_output: git lfs install && git lfs track "*.gguf"

title: Clone and pull behavior
description: Clones fetch pointers then download LFS content (all or recent, configurable); GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE skips downloads for metadata-only work. Fetch policy controls bandwidth. Smudge filters materialize files.

title: Locking binary files
description: git lfs lock marks a binary as exclusively edited; others see the lock and avoid merge conflicts. Locking replaces merging for unmergeable files. The workflow is lock-edit-push-unlock.

demo.program: print('git lfs lock model.gguf  # exclusive edit')
demo.expected_output: git lfs lock model.gguf  # exclusive edit

title: The batch API
description: LFS uses a batch API to negotiate uploads/downloads with the server, enabling parallel transfers and resumability. The protocol is HTTPS + JSON. Understanding it helps debug server issues.

title: Pruning local objects
description: git lfs prune removes old local LFS objects not needed by current history, reclaiming disk. Local caches grow; prune periodically. Disk hygiene matters.

title: Migrating history to LFS
description: git lfs migrate import rewrites history moving big files to LFS (with --everything for all branches). History rewrite requires team coordination. Migrate once, benefit forever.

title: Verifying LFS integrity
description: git lfs fsck checks object integrity; git lfs ls-files shows tracked files and their status. Verification commands exist. Trust but verify.

title: When not to use LFS
description: For datasets, consider DVC or object storage with manifests; LFS fits model weights and binaries versioned alongside code. Right tool per artifact. LFS is for code-adjacent binaries.

title: Common pitfalls
description: Forgetting git lfs install on a new machine, tracking after committing big files, and pushing without LFS server access are the classics. The checklist prevents them. Onboarding docs should include LFS.
